title: V(a) and V(b) are disjoint iff a + b is the unit ideal
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $\mathfrak a,\mathfrak b\subseteq R$ ideals. Then $V(\mathfrak a)\cap V(\mathfrak b)=\emptyset$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ if and only if $\mathfrak a+\mathfrak b=R$, that is, if and only if there are $x\in\mathfrak a$ and $y\in\mathfrak b$ with $x+y=1$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology), parts (8) (V(I) is empty iff I is the unit ideal) and (10) (the intersection of the V(I_a) is V of the union, i.e. V(a) ∩ V(b) = V(a + b)); used in the proof of More on Algebra Lemma Tag 07M3
